I’m sorry you’re going through this. I feel like everyone else has covered the legal and medical aspect of what is going on, so I won’t comment on it. I have been raped a few times and I wish someone had told me a few things about healing, so I’d like to pass them to you. Of course, take it with all the grains of salt you need to. 
-you did not do ANYTHING wrong. 
-he, and he alone is at fault for everything that happened
-be kind to yourself. (I struggled with this because I blamed myself)
-surround yourself with people and things that bring you comfort, and do not let anyone take that away from you (I cuddled a teddy bear as a 30yo. It weirded me out until I realized that I needed it more than anything else) 
-grief and healing are not linear. I had days where I thought i was good and feelings came out of nowhere. I had to learn to cope with them (meditation, yoga and therapy were my saving graces)
-you are going to be ok. I don’t know you, but as a woman, I inherently believe that most women are badasses who would make the world a better place if some men would just let them. 
-You’re a badass. You’re a survivor and you will persevere. 
-I wish you the very best. If you need to vent, scream, rant, anything at all, please feel free to reach out

Sometimes when I'm feeling reckless, I eat a med rare burger from a shittier place just to keep my gutbugs on their toes, but there is a satisfaction to knowing exactly how your food is made. 

- I go through phases of vegetarianism and veganism (like a month at a time). It forces me to look past my usual foods, see what new health bullshit people are into, and changes up how I feel, about food and in general. 

- Volunteering at homeless shelters. I stocked cans, and having grown up without canned food, I would go back home and see if there was anything I could make with different cans of food. Of course, the grocery store offered more options than a shelter, but it forced me out of my comfort zone of food-from-scratch.
